source: ESPN public injury report and game summaries

injuries.name: T.J. McConnell
injuries.short_comment: McConnell (hamstring) is listed as out for Sunday's game in New York.
injuries.long_comment: McConnell missed the Pacers' first nine games of the 2026-27 campaign because of a right hamstring issue. However, he exited Friday's 128-119 loss to the Cavaliers due to left hamstring soreness. McConnell will have another opportunity to play Monday versus Oklahoma City, but for now, he should be considered day-to-day. In the meantime, Quenton Jackson is in line for more minutes behind Andrew Nembhard.

injuries.name: Pascal Siakam
injuries.short_comment: Siakam (hip) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against New York.
injuries.long_comment: Siakam has only missed one game this season, but he's in danger of sitting out Sunday due to left hip soreness. If the 32-year-old can't suit up versus the Knicks, Obi Toppin may move into the starting lineup.

injuries.name: Tyrese Haliburton
injuries.short_comment: Haliburton (hamstring) is expected to miss at least two more weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injuries.long_comment: Haliburton hasn't played since Oct. 26 due to a left hamstring strain, and the Pacers won't rush him back. With the star floor general unlikely to return until mid-December at the earliest, Quenton Jackson and T.J. McConnell are candidates for increased playing time, while Andrew Nembhard figures to continue seeing increased playmaking duties.

injuries.name: Ben Sheppard
injuries.short_comment: Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
injuries.long_comment: Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

injuries.name: Johnny Furphy
injuries.short_comment: Furphy (knee) is practicing with the G League's Noblesville Boom, per Alex Golden of SI.com.
injuries.long_comment: The Pacers have been pretty quiet regarding Furphy's ACL recovery since the offseason, but it's encouraging to hear some form of progress as the forward begins to ramp up his activity. Although Furphy still lacks a firm timetable for a return and is likely to be brought back slowly, it appears a season debut before the start of the new calendar year is in the cards.

injuries.name: Jordan Clarkson
injuries.short_comment: Clarkson (foot) won't play in Saturday's game against Portland.
injuries.long_comment: Clarkson is battling a case of plantar fasciitis in his right foot, so he will miss a second consecutive contest. Without Clarkson on the floor, Landry Shamet is in line for more playing time.

injuries.name: Karl-Anthony Towns
injuries.short_comment: Towns (illness) won't play in Saturday's game versus the Trail Blazers.
injuries.long_comment: Towns was initially listed as questionable. However, he has since been ruled out, marking his first absence of the 2026-27 campaign. Towns' next opportunity to play will come Sunday against Indiana. In the meantime, Andre Drummond is in line to start.

injuries.name: OG Anunoby
injuries.short_comment: Anunoby (calf) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Trail Blazers.
injuries.long_comment: Anunoby will miss his first game of the 2026-27 regular season due to left calf tightness, although he could be back on the floor for the second leg of the Knicks' back-to-back set against the Pacers on Sunday. Landry Shamet and Miles McBride are both in line for elevated roles in Anunoby's absence.
